feedback.problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=(x-2){y}^{2}.$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)\le 0?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=2$ and $y=0.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below. Since we have an "or equal to" inequality, we use solid lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065421/assets/3222e808ccb652a4bfb3b3291099b87f5a1db5d4d38635d58c6649d8efc71f06.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065421/assets/e8ab67f737067fb0e0bfc64a8060fdefacf79ba430bdf9a24d21dbc7893b1cf7.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $(x-2)$ | ${y}^{2}$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-left | $(1,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Top-Right | $(3,1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(1,-1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(3,-1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y)\le 0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065421/assets/42e3960fe067a02d6263df15ede7224ecd6b977c744139889d83529d873096bf.png)
